extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, journal editors, and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and argumentation about providing credit, visibility, and incentive mechanisms for scholarly peer reviewing so as to improve review uptake, quality, and transparency across academic publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition/credit for peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly peer reviewers get limited recognition for performing ... quality control; reviewers receive little tangible benefits apart from a sense of altruistic satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate credit and visibility to improve and motivate peer review activity; acknowledge and reward reviewers for their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reviewers' time and workload when assigning credit
rubrics_metrics.description: An average peer reviewer may review several manuscripts a year ... a considerable amount of time is spent in doing this critical activity with little tangible benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems of credit should reflect the time and intellectual effort invested by reviewers so that reviewing is a recognized scholarly contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate reviewer selection bias by journal reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many reviewers may not be willing to review at all for new or low impact factor journals or do a very superficial job for these journals but carry out more elaborate reviews for reputed journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives/credit mechanisms should reduce the disparity in willingness and effort between high- and low-impact journals to avoid unequal standards of publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforms to showcase reviews as scientific output
rubrics_metrics.description: Networking sites such as Publons, PubPeer, and Faculty of 1000 have been launched with the aim of providing platforms to showcase one's reviews as scientific output and enhance its visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage use of such platforms so reviewers can publicly demonstrate their reviewing activity as part of scholarly output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reviews citable (DOIs for reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some platforms (e.g., Publons) issue digital object identifiers for reviews rendering them citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign persistent identifiers to reviews so they become formally citable contributions in curricula vitae, grant applications, and academic dossiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and verify peer review output
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms allow one to record and verify the peer review output based on which reviewer scores are assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt verified recording of review activity (with verification mechanisms) so institutions can trust and use review records in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring/metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer scores are assigned based on recorded and verified peer review output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop transparent, fair reviewer metrics that reflect quality and quantity of reviewing rather than raw counts alone; ensure scoring systems are interpretable and not easily gamed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow inclusion of peer review output in career evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded review activity and scores can subsequently be mentioned when applying for research grants, faculty, or editorial positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and funders should accept and weigh peer review contributions as part of hiring, promotion, and grant review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency and accountability in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: These initiatives are much needed to increase transparency, accountability, and credit for the peer reviewing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote openness (where appropriate) so reviews are open to scrutiny, which can deter misconduct and poor-quality reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review to reduce abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Open review would reduce an important shortcoming of the peer review process – the abuse of peer review – by making the review open to scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider open or published reviewer comments to expose and discourage unethical or abusive use of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share reviewer insights to catalyze further research
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas and insights provided by a reviewer of a scientific manuscript may serve to catalyze further and better-designed work in the area but ... closed peer review ensures that the reviewer comments never reach the larger academic community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reviewer comments more visible (with appropriate protections) so useful critique and suggestions can disseminate and stimulate subsequent research and cross-talk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional responsibility to acknowledge and reward reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The academia must take steps to acknowledge and reward the work of peer reviewers and provide better visibility to their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities, journals, and funders should create formal recognition/reward mechanisms (e.g., credit frameworks, inclusion in evaluations) to improve review quality, researcher communication, and advancement of science.
